title: Transition endomorphism 1 − s of the product of an inverse system
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category], let $(K_n,f_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system of objects of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-inverse-system], and assume that the product $P=\prod_{n\geq1}K_n$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_n:P\to K_n$ exists [def-weil-category-product]. The *shift* $s:P\to P$ is the unique morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ s=f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ for every $n$, and the *transition endomorphism* is $1-s=\mathrm{id}_P-s$, equivalently the unique morphism satisfying $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ for every $n$. If $(\varphi_n):(K_n,f_n)\to(K'_n,f'_n)$ is a morphism of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] and both products $P=\prod_nK_n$ and $P'=\prod_nK'_n$ exist, then $(1-s')\circ\prod_n\varphi_n=\prod_n\varphi_n\circ(1-s)$; after composing with $\mathrm{pr}'_n$, this equality is exactly $f'_n\circ\varphi_{n+1}=\varphi_n\circ f_n$ for every $n$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Definition 13.34.1 (Tag 08TC), derived.tex line 10442: "the map $\prod K_n\to\prod K_n$ is given by $(k_n)\mapsto(k_n-f_{n+1}(k_{n+1}))$" (Stacks indexes the transition map $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ as $f_{n+1}$); Bhatt-Scholze, arXiv:1309.1198v2, Proposition 3.1.10, p. 17 (the map $t-\mathrm{id}$)
